title: Concept of Political Science
shortDescription: What political science studies: state, power, sovereignty, theories of the state and forms of government.
genZNote: Politics isn't just elections — it's who gets power, how they keep it and why anyone obeys. This chapter is the vocabulary pack for everything else.

sections.heading: Meaning and Scope
bullets: Political science studies the state, government, power, politics and public policy; Aristotle is called the father of political science ("Man is a political animal").
Branches: political theory, comparative politics, public administration, international relations, political economy.
Indian roots: Kautilya's Arthashastra (statecraft), Ashokan edicts, ideas of dharma and rajdharma.

sections.heading: State, Nation and Sovereignty
sections.body: Theories of origin of the state: divine right, force, social contract (Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau), evolutionary/historical.

table.caption: Key concepts
rows: A community with shared identity, history or culture
Supreme authority — internal (within territory) and external (independence)
Ability to influence; recognised right to command; acceptance by the governed

sections.heading: Forms and Systems of Government
bullets: Monarchy, oligarchy, democracy; unitary vs federal; parliamentary vs presidential.
India: sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic with a parliamentary federal system (Preamble).
Separation of powers: legislature, executive, judiciary (Montesquieu).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Political science is the systematic study of the state, power and government, including how authority is justified and organised.

commonTraps: Do not call government and state the same thing.

confusedTerms.distinction: The state is permanent and sovereign; governments change.

sources.name: NCERT, Indian Constitution at Work (Class XI Political Science)
Constitution of India (official text), Legislative Department

questions.prompt: Which is NOT an essential element of the state?
questions.explanation: The four elements are population, territory, government and sovereignty.
